title: 2026 Minnesota gubernatorial election
description: Minnesota will elect its next governor in 2026, with the governor serving as chief executive of the state and overseeing the budget, agencies, and implementation of state law. The race is likely to center on taxes, education, public safety, abortion, and state spending, reflecting broader partisan debates in Minnesota. Ballotpedia says general-election candidates will be added after the primaries, and the Minnesota Secretary of State is the official source for candidate filings and election information. Tim Walz is the incumbent governor, but available sources here do not establish that he is on the 2026 ballot.
polling_note: No public polling found for this race in the last 90 days as of 2026-05-17.

candidates.name: Jeff Johnson
candidates.summary: Jeff Johnson is a Minnesota Republican politician who served in the Minnesota House of Representatives from 2001 to 2007 and on the Hennepin County Board from 2009 to 2021. He was the Republican nominee for governor in 2014 and 2018 and announced another gubernatorial campaign in 2025.

Economy.stance: Jeff Johnson says Minnesota is overtaxing businesses and households and argues for lower spending, more efficiency, and reduced fraud. He frames business retention and fiscal restraint as central to improving the state economy.

sources.title: St. Cloud Republican Jeff Johnson announces Minnesota governor bid

Abortion & Reproductive Health.stance: Jeff Johnson describes himself as strongly anti-abortion and says he is '100% unapologetically pro life starting at conception.'

Firearms & Second Amendment.stance: Jeff Johnson supports an optional Minnesota Citizens Enhanced Protection Act that would provide additional training for permit holders. He presents the proposal as a training and preparedness measure rather than a broad gun restriction.

sources.title: St. Cloud Republican Jeff Johnson announces Minnesota governor bid

Immigration.stance: Jeff Johnson supports stricter enforcement against illegal immigration, says he has no problem with deporting people who are in the country illegally, and distinguishes that from legal immigration. He has also criticized sanctuary-style cooperation limits and previously proposed a refugee moratorium in St. Cloud.

Civil Rights & Equality.stance: Jeff Johnson opposes transgender women and girls using female bathrooms, locker rooms, prisons, and sports, and he says he would end taxpayer-funded DEI programs. He has also criticized drag performances at the state Capitol and gender-affirming care for minors.

Election Policy.stance: Jeff Johnson supports requiring photo identification to vote as part of election-integrity measures.

Healthcare.stance: Jeff Johnson says he opposes taxpayer-funded healthcare for undocumented immigrants and favors limiting government involvement in health care. His public comments emphasize cost control, private-market approaches, and opposition to expanding public programs.

candidates.name: Kobey Layne
candidates.summary: Kobey Layne is a Republican candidate in Minnesota’s 2026 governor race. His campaign website says he is a public policy graduate, holds a Master of Public Policy degree, and previously worked as a legislative assistant in the Minnesota Senate; Ballotpedia also lists retail work among his career experience.

Healthcare.stance: Supports Medicare for All and says it would protect healthcare access for people with disabilities, older adults, farmers, families, the self-employed, and small businesses. He also says Minnesota should protect and fund Section 340B to help hospitals avoid closures.

Economy.stance: Supports worker cooperatives, including grants or loans for startup and conversion costs, technical assistance for co-ops and small businesses, and a revolving loan fund for worker co-ops. He also backs universal childcare and tax policies such as a wealth tax and higher rates on very high incomes.

Climate/Energy.stance: Supports a moratorium on new data center construction until Minnesota adopts a stronger regulatory framework. He also backs a Prove It First mining standard, stricter permitting for nonferrous mining, and upfront financial assurance for cleanup costs.

Abortion & Reproductive Health.stance: Supports abortion access, contraception, and birth control as part of a single-payer health care system. His campaign also calls for comprehensive sex education that includes contraception education.

Immigration.stance: Says he would work with the Minnesota Attorney General to prosecute ICE officers and frames the issue as community protection and accountability in immigration enforcement.

Foreign Policy.stance: Supports divesting Minnesota state pension funds from companies that facilitate Israeli settlements or military supplies to Israel, and opposes state contracts with companies that sell to Israeli settlements. His campaign also calls for repealing a state contracting restriction related to Israel.

Civil Rights & Equality.stance: Supports LGBTQIA2S+ protections, including preserving gender-affirming care, sealing name-change records for some transgender people, prohibiting gender discrimination in shelters, protecting trans students in schools, and expanding LGBTQIA2S+-inclusive sex education.

Election Policy.stance: Supports making Election Day a state holiday, establishing ranked-choice voting in state elections, and placing gubernatorial term limits in the Minnesota Constitution.

Local Issues.stance: Supports rental assistance, a 3% annual cap on rent increases, stronger tenant protections and tenant unions, limits on large-scale housing purchases, and more funding for Housing Infrastructure Bonds.

Education.stance: Supports raising teacher pay, protecting educators’ ability to teach Minnesota, U.S., and world history including LGBTQIA2S+ and Black history, indexing school funding to inflation, expanding trades and skills programs, and funding youth mentorship programs.

reviews.summary: This is a well-sourced and professionally compiled profile of the 2026 Minnesota gubernatorial race. The profile demonstrates strong research across three major candidates with appropriate differentiation between candidates with extensive legislative/executive records (Walz) versus newer or less-established candidates (Layne). Sourcing is robust: Tim Walz's issue positions are backed by official press releases and news coverage from reputable outlets; Jeff Johnson's positions cite recent announcements and policy repositories; Kobey Layne's stances are drawn directly from his official campaign website. Candidate backgrounds are internally consistent with cited sources, and the distinction between "no public position found" (a legitimate absence) and substantive positions is properly maintained. The profile appropriately documents Tim Walz's decision not to seek reelection while noting polling still includes him. Language remains neutral across partisan divides, with stance descriptions avoiding loaded terminology. Minor areas for improvement noted below do not substantially undermine profile quality.

flags.concern: The profile notes that Tim Walz announced he would not seek a third term. My training data suggests he has previously expressed interest in various political paths, and while this statement is backed by the provided URL, a human reviewer should confirm this specific 'not seeking re-election' status remains the current official stance as of mid-2026.
flags.suggestion: Verify the status of the governor's 2026 ballot filing or withdrawal declaration at the Minnesota Secretary of State’s official portal.

flags.concern: The poll lists a 2026-01-30 matchup between Tim Walz and Jeff Johnson. Given the conflicting information regarding Governor Walz's candidacy, this poll should be treated as a snapshot of hypothetical or early-cycle data.

The education section lists the years for degrees as 'null'. While accurate to the provided sources, a quick check could verify if those dates are retrievable from university directories for better completeness.
flags.suggestion: If available, add graduation years for the J.D. and B.A. programs to improve detail.

reviews.summary: This profile is exceptionally well-structured and demonstrates high-quality research practices. The candidate backgrounds are detailed and consistently supported by official government links and reputable news sources. The summary of policy positions is balanced, and the profile correctly identifies where public information is absent (noting low confidence in those areas) rather than attempting to fabricate stances. The distinction between incumbent status, past legislative history, and current campaign platforms is clearly maintained throughout.

Strong, well-sourced profile with consistent internal sourcing across all candidates. Tim Walz’s section is particularly robust, with high-confidence issue stances backed by official Minnesota government press releases and credible news outlets. Jeff Johnson and Kobey Layne sections are also well-documented using campaign websites, Ballotpedia, and news coverage. Neutral language is maintained throughout with no partisan framing or loaded terminology. Gaps (e.g., “No public position found”) are appropriately noted after apparent good-faith searches.

forecast.rationale: There is no usable public head-to-head polling in the provided race data, and the current candidate list includes only Republican candidates while no Democratic general-election candidate is established here. With sparse race-specific evidence, confidence must be low. Minnesota has been a competitive but generally Democratic-leaning statewide environment in recent cycles, and the incumbent governor is a Democrat, though the provided data does not establish that he is seeking reelection. Given that party context modestly favors Democrats but the field is incomplete and polling is absent, the most defensible informational rating is Tilt Democratic.
